name: Local Color Transfer Detection
description: Detects localized color transfer applied to harmonize AI-generated content with surrounding regions (Reinhard et al., 2001).
mechanism:
This method detects localized color transfer operations — commonly used in image compositing and AI content harmonization — by analyzing statistical inconsistencies in color distributions:

1. **Lαβ Color Space Decomposition**: The image is converted to the decorrelated Lαβ color space (Ruderman, 1998), which minimizes cross-channel correlation and isolates luminance from chrominance. In this space, color transfer operations modifying mean and standard deviation become linear transformations: t(x) = (σ_t/σ_s)(x − μ_s) + μ_t, where μ and σ are the mean and standard deviation of source (s) and target (t) regions.

2. **Local Statistical Consistency Analysis**: The image is divided into overlapping blocks (32×32 to 64×64 pixels). For each block, the mean and standard deviation of each Lαβ channel are computed. In an authentic photograph, adjacent blocks sharing similar scene content should have smooth transitions in their color statistics. The method detects abrupt changes in per-block (μ, σ) that indicate boundary regions where color transfer was applied to harmonize a spliced or AI-generated region.

3. **Inter-Channel Correlation Mapping**: In natural images, the correlations between L, α, and β channels follow scene-dependent but locally consistent patterns. Color transfer operations disrupt these correlations because they independently scale each channel. The method computes the 3×3 correlation matrix for each block and identifies regions where the correlation structure deviates significantly from neighboring blocks, using the Frobenius norm of the correlation matrix difference.

4. **Illuminant Color Estimation**: Color transfer can introduce illuminant inconsistencies. The method estimates the local illuminant color using Gray-World and Max-RGB algorithms in each block. In an unmanipulated photograph under a single light source, all blocks should estimate similar illuminant colors. Regions with divergent illuminant estimates indicate either mixed lighting or artificial color adjustment.
parameters:
Color space: Lαβ (decorrelated)
Block size: 32×32 or 64×64 pixels
Block overlap: 50%
Correlation matrix comparison: Frobenius norm
Illuminant estimation: Gray-World + Max-RGB
Statistical change threshold: > 2σ from local neighborhood mean
Minimum image size: 128×128 pixels
accuracy: 79–87% detection accuracy for color-transferred regions. Illuminant inconsistency detection achieves F1-score of 0.82 for splicing detection. Inter-channel correlation analysis adds 4–6% improvement over statistics-only approach. False positive rate of 7% in images with strong natural color gradients (sunsets, mixed lighting).
source: Reinhard, E. et al. (2001). Color Transfer between Images. IEEE Computer Graphics and Applications, 21(5), 34–41.
useCase: Detecting color harmonization applied to AI-inpainted or composited regions. Identifying images where color adjustment was used to blend spliced content. Analyzing illuminant consistency for forgery localization. Detecting AI-generated images with post-processed color grading.
strengths:
• Lαβ space provides decorrelated channels ideal for transfer detection
• Color transfer leaves characteristic statistical signatures detectable at block level
• Illuminant estimation provides physics-based evidence of manipulation
• Method is robust to JPEG compression and image resizing
• Works without reference images or source material
limitations:
• Natural color gradients (sunsets, studio lighting) can trigger false positives
• Global color adjustments (white balance correction) are indistinguishable from legitimate editing
• Small transferred regions (< 32×32 pixels) fall below block resolution
• HDR tone mapping creates inter-channel decorrelations similar to color transfer
• AI generators that directly produce harmonized output bypass detectable transfer operations
